code:
# A KL-divergence loss should be exactly 0 comparing a distribution to itself
kl = my_custom_kl_divergence(p, p)
assert torch.allclose(kl, torch.tensor(0.0), atol=1e-6)

# Custom autograd.Function backward: check against finite differences
from torch.autograd import gradcheck
x = torch.randn(4, 4, dtype=torch.double, requires_grad=True)
assert gradcheck(MyCustomFunction.apply, (x,), eps=1e-6, atol=1e-4)
caption: Neither check needs to know the "right" output -- only a known value or an internal consistency property.

eyebrow: Overfit one tiny batch before trusting the full run
code:
tiny_batch = next(iter(loader))
for step in range(200):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss = compute_loss(model, tiny_batch)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
print(f"Loss after 200 steps on 1 batch: {loss.item():.6f}")
# Should be ~0. If not, the pipeline is broken before "does it generalize" matters.
caption: This doesn't test generalization -- it tests that gradients are flowing and nothing upstream is silently broken.
